findings.premise: The design narrows BOTH consumers of the Story's range — the subject's changed set (changedFiles' committed-range branch) and the degraded grounding's rangeDiff — to the Story's own change units, and adds the reviewer cwd fix. Together these cover both root causes the ISSUE names.
findings.evidence: ISSUE rootCause (1) names the base..HEAD range read by resolveStoryRangeBase and assembleDiffCodeReviewGrounding; (2) names CliProvider.complete calling runClaude(args, prompt) with no exec override. In the code, the subject's changed set comes from changedFiles (subject.ts:114-126, which passes the range base), and that function's committed branch is `collectDiff(repoPath, { from: opts.base, ...globs }, ranged)` (changed-files.ts:144). The grounding range is `rangeDiff(...) { return runDiff(repoPath, { from: base, ...excludeInput(excludeGlobs) }) }` (grounding.ts:364-366). The design changes all three sites (2.3, 2.4, 2.7-2.9). The fix intent's 'merge committed on its own' part is enforced by the merge-in-progress gate (2.10) plus the prompt rule (2.11). Fast-forward and committed-squash integrations are a declared known limit that tests pin; they are not silently dropped. findings.premise: The merge gate sites handleImplement / handleValidate exist and can gate before any prompt render or record write, including the standalone path that renders renderStandaloneImplementPrompt.
findings.evidence: handleImplement (src/mcp/build-step/phases/implement.ts:42) resolves repoPath first (:45). It then branches early to handleStandaloneImplement (:53-55), before noteBuildStart (:74) and renderImplementPrompt (:87). handleValidate is at validate.ts:140. A gate placed right after resolveRepoPath therefore covers both the plan and standalone paths. One detail matters: the gate must go BEFORE the standalone early return, or standalone builds escape it. findings.premise: Ledger exclusion is done by git through git_diff's exclude (LEDGER_EXCLUDE_GLOBS) for the review set and grounding, while the BUILD changeLog uses exact-path exclusions only. Keeping exclude on every per-unit call and intersecting after git's exclusion therefore preserves both.
findings.evidence: changed-files.ts:55-60 defines LEDGER_EXCLUDE_GLOBS, forwarded as `{ exclude: [...opts.excludeGlobs] }` to every diff (:122-128, :144). Before the git_diff call, pathspecArgs emits `:(top,exclude,glob)` entries (diff.ts:203-207). validate.ts:363-366 calls collectBuildChangeLog with `exclude: [own.json, own.md, buildStartRelPath(...)]` and base, with no globs, and collectBuildChangeLog forwards only base/exclude (changed-files.ts:188-191). The design intersects with storyChangeSet.paths after the existing git-excluded diff and before `keep`, so the exclusion order is unchanged. summary.prose: A Story's code review now looks only at what the Story itself changed. Its changes are its own non-merge first-parent commits since its range base plus any edits made inside a merge commit; the reviewed diff carries only those changes, so a mid-build merge of upstream code no longer floods the review and no merged-in line reaches the reviewer. Build turns refuse to run while a merge is in progress, so every merge is committed before the next round of Story changes. The reviewer's model calls now start in the reviewed repository instead of the daemon's own checkout.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Make Story code review read the Story's own changes in the reviewed repository

api.name: storyChangeSet

returns.meaning: The Story's own change units since the base, in first-parent order. A 'commit' unit is each commit from `git rev-list --first-parent --no-merges <base>..HEAD` (from = its parent, or the empty tree for a root commit; paths from `git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r --root`). A 'merge-edit' unit is each first-parent merge M whose committed tree differs from the clean auto-merge of its two parents: auto = the tree printed by `git merge-tree --write-tree M^1 M^2` (conflicted or not), from = auto, to = M, paths = `git diff --name-only auto M`. That difference is exactly what was edited inside the merge commit (Story edits folded in, or a conflict resolution). `paths` is the sorted union of all units' paths. `sharedPaths` are the paths that are also in some merge's merged-in side (`git diff --name-only M^1 auto`). `foldedPaths` are the paths of merge-edit units. An octopus merge (three or more parents), whose auto-merge merge-tree cannot compute, becomes ONE merge-edit unit over its whole change (from = M^1, to = M) with a warn log: the set over-includes rather than drops anything.

errors.condition: A git command fails (for example, the base cannot be resolved) — the same condition under which today's base..HEAD diff already fails.

preconditions: repoPath is a git work tree.
postconditions: No path appears that only a merge's merged-in side changed.
Edits made inside a merge commit are never silently dropped: they are a merge-edit unit.
Read-only: it never changes the repository (merge-tree --write-tree writes only objects, never refs, the index or the working tree).
It applies no exclusions itself: its consumers keep excluding through git (git_diff exclude), so there is still one implementation of the glob semantics.

api.name: mergeInProgress

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: The repository the build turn runs in.

returns.meaning: true when a merge has been started and not yet committed: `git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD` succeeds, or the file at `git rev-parse --git-path SQUASH_MSG` exists (a `git merge --squash` not yet committed).

postconditions: A git failure other than 'MERGE_HEAD not found' is logged and treated as false, so it never blocks a build on its own.

api.name: changedFiles
api.signature: export async function changedFiles(repoPath: string, opts?: ChangedFilesOptions): Promise<readonly string[]>

parameters.name: opts
parameters.purpose: Unchanged shape. With opts.base on a clean tree, the committed-range branch still runs its existing git_diff {from: base, exclude: opts.excludeGlobs} (so the ledger exclusions stay in git, as today), and the result is then intersected with storyChangeSet(repoPath, base).paths before the existing `keep` filter.

returns.meaning: The working-tree set when the tree is dirty (unchanged); otherwise the Story's own paths since the base. This also narrows the BUILD record's body.changeLog, which collectBuildChangeLog derives through changedFiles with the range base (validate.ts, completion-record.ts): the ledger then lists the Story's own files, not files a merge brought in. That is intended.

errors.condition: git failure, as before, including a storyChangeSet failure.

postconditions: Without opts.base the result is byte-for-byte what it was before.

api.name: realDiffGroundingDeps

returns.meaning: Its rangeDiff(repoPath, base, excludeGlobs) now computes storyChangeSet(repoPath, base). Every git_diff call below carries the same exclude: excludeGlobs, so the ledger exclusions apply to each one exactly as they do today. Paths no merge touched get one net diff: git_diff {from: base, paths: <those>, exclude}. Each shared path gets only the Story's own hunks: for every unit that touched it, in order, git_diff {from: unit.from, to: unit.to, paths: [<shared paths of that unit>], exclude}. rangeDiff splits every call's body per file itself and returns the per-file text in DiffResult.hunksByFile: a path seen in several calls gets their sections appended in unit order, never overwritten, and a folded path's own entry starts with '[edited inside merge commit <short sha>]'. files has one entry per path; truncated is true if any call was truncated. When the change set is empty it returns an empty DiffResult without calling git_diff.

errors.condition: storyChangeSet or a git_diff call fails; the assembler's existing step-down applies.

postconditions: Every file in the range result is a Story path, so the byte bound is spent only on Story files.
No hunk line comes from a merge's merged-in side.

api.name: gitDiffTool
api.signature: input: { cwd: string; from?: string; to?: string; staged?: boolean; path?: string; paths?: readonly string[]; exclude?: readonly string[]; maxBytes?: number }

parameters.name: paths
parameters.purpose:
New: repo-root-relative positive pathspecs, emitted as ':(top,literal)

' after '--'. Combines with from/to and exclude. Mutually exclusive with path (both set is invalid-input).

returns.meaning: Unchanged shape; the body and the file list cover only the given paths.

errors.condition: paths is not an array of non-empty strings, is empty, or is given together with path.

postconditions: Without paths the git command line is exactly as before.

api.name: buildDiffSymbols

parameters.name: diff
parameters.purpose: The resolved diff; may now carry hunksByFile.

returns.meaning: Unchanged shape. A file's hunk text is diff.hunksByFile.get(path) when hunksByFile is present, else splitDiffByFile(diff.body) as today.

postconditions: Without hunksByFile the result is exactly as before.
With hunksByFile no section is overwritten and every marker stays on its own file.

api.name: CliProvider.completeStructured
api.signature: completeStructured<T>(messages: LLMMessage[], schema: StructuredSchema, opts?: StructuredCompletionOpts): Promise<T>

parameters.name: opts.cwd
parameters.purpose: New: working directory for the claude/codex subprocess. Passed as the ExecOverride {cwd, timeoutMs: this.timeoutMs} to runClaude/runCodex.

postconditions: When opts.cwd is undefined, runClaude/runCodex are called with no override, exactly as before.

api.name: CliProvider.complete
postconditions: When opts.cwd is undefined, behaviour is unchanged.

api.name: judgeAdherence / judgeConventions / judgeCoverage / judgeFunctionalCoverage / judgeQuality

returns.meaning: Unchanged; each judge's completeStructured call now passes { cwd: subject.repoPath }.

postconditions: The reviewer's subprocess starts in the reviewed repository.

api.name: handleImplement / handleValidate

returns.meaning: When mergeInProgress(repoPath) is true, returns { next: 'error', error: { code: 'merge-in-progress', message: <commit the merge on its own, then retry>, retryable: true } } before any other work.

errors.condition: A merge has been started and not committed.

postconditions: No implement or validate turn runs on top of an uncommitted merge.

api.name: implement prompts (implement-task.md, renderStandaloneImplementPrompt)

returns.meaning: Each implement prompt gains one rule: to bring upstream changes in during the Story, merge with `git merge --no-ff` (or `git pull --no-rebase --no-ff`), commit the merge on its own before any further Story change, and never squash-merge or fast-forward upstream into the Story.

postconditions: The implementer is told the one integration form the review can separate from Story work.

dataModelChanges.details: cwd?: string | undefined — working directory for subprocess-backed providers; OllamaProvider ignores it.
readonly cwd?: string | undefined — same meaning.
paths?: readonly string[] — positive repo-root pathspecs.
hunksByFile?: ReadonlyMap<string, string> — per-file hunk text already split by the producer; buildDiffSymbols prefers it over splitting body.

errorCases.scenario: The range base cannot be resolved (rewritten history, shallow clone).
errorCases.detection: git rev-list in storyChangeSet exits non-zero; the helper throws NoBuildChangesError (changedFiles) or DiffUnavailableError (rangeDiff).
errorCases.response: The callers' existing step-down runs: resolveCodeReviewSubject and assembleDiffCodeReviewGrounding fall back to their plainer attempts, as they do today for a bad base.
errorCases.userImpact: Same as today for a bad base: the subject steps down to the no-base derivation, which on a clean tree is empty, while the grounding steps down to the last commit. This Story does not change that path; the warn log names the failed attempt.

errorCases.scenario: A merge is in progress when a build turn is called.
errorCases.response: handleImplement / handleValidate return error 'merge-in-progress' (retryable) before rendering a prompt, running checks or writing any record.
errorCases.userImpact: The user commits the merge on its own, then retries the turn.

errorCases.scenario: git itself cannot be run while checking for a merge (not a repo, git missing).
errorCases.detection: execFileSync throws with an error other than exit status 1.
errorCases.response: Log a warning and return false; the turn's own later git use surfaces the real failure.
errorCases.userImpact: None from the gate; it never blocks a build by itself.

errorCases.scenario: git_diff receives paths together with path, or an empty or non-string paths array.
errorCases.detection: Input validation in gitDiffTool.execute, alongside the existing exclude check.
errorCases.userImpact: A programming error is reported instead of silently diffing the whole repository.

edgeCases.input: The Story's range holds no non-merge first-parent commit (only a merge, or nothing).
edgeCases.expected: storyChangeSet has no units; changedFiles returns []; rangeDiff returns an empty DiffResult without calling git_diff. The review sees an empty change set rather than the merge's files.

edgeCases.input: A Story commit deleted a file.
edgeCases.expected: The path is in the change set and shows as deleted in the range diff.

edgeCases.input: A file was changed both by a Story commit and by the merge.
edgeCases.expected: The file is in the set and in sharedPaths; its hunk text is the Story's own per-unit diffs for that file, with no line from the merge's merged-in side.

edgeCases.input: A merged-in upstream file that no Story commit touched.
edgeCases.expected: Absent from both the changed set and the reviewed hunks.
Unchanged: the working-tree set is used and the base is not consulted.

edgeCases.input: The range base is the repository's root commit's parent (empty tree) or the first Story commit is a root commit.
edgeCases.expected: diff-tree is run with --root so a root commit's files are listed.

edgeCases.input: A path containing glob characters or spaces.
edgeCases.expected: Passed as a ':(top,literal)' pathspec, so it matches only itself.

edgeCases.input: completeStructured / complete called without opts.cwd (every non-review caller).
edgeCases.expected: runClaude / runCodex are called with no ExecOverride, exactly as before.

edgeCases.input: The Story branch was merged into main by the user and HEAD is on main after a fast-forward.
edgeCases.expected: First-parent history still runs through the Story's commits, so they are listed.

edgeCases.input: Story edits staged into a merge commit (or amended into it) after the merge.
edgeCases.expected: git merge-tree's clean auto-merge differs from the merge commit on those files, so they form a merge-edit unit: they are in the change set, reviewed with the hunks auto..M, and marked '[edited inside merge commit <sha>]'.

edgeCases.input: A merge with conflicts that were resolved by hand.
edgeCases.expected: The resolution differs from merge-tree's conflicted auto-merge, so the resolved files form a merge-edit unit and the resolution is reviewed.

edgeCases.input: collectBuildChangeLog with a range base after a mid-build merge.
edgeCases.expected: The BUILD record's changeLog lists only the Story's own paths.

edgeCases.input: KNOWN LIMIT — upstream brought in by a fast-forward (git pull / git merge with no merge commit) during the Story.
edgeCases.expected: The upstream commits are first-parent non-merge commits and are counted as Story work; nothing in git marks them as foreign. The implement prompts tell the implementer to merge with --no-ff instead. A test pins this behaviour so a later fix is a visible change.

edgeCases.input: KNOWN LIMIT — upstream squash-merged (git merge --squash) and committed during the Story.
edgeCases.expected: While the squash is uncommitted (SQUASH_MSG present) build turns refuse with merge-in-progress. Once committed, the squash commit is an ordinary commit and is counted as Story work. The implement prompts forbid squash-merging upstream. A test pins this behaviour.

edgeCases.input: Two Story commits touch the same shared path, and a folded path is not the first file in a diff body.
edgeCases.expected: The shared path's hunk text holds both commits' sections in order; the folded path's marker heads that path's own text.

edgeCases.input: The range holds an octopus merge (three or more parents).
edgeCases.expected: No throw: the merge's whole change (M^1..M) is one merge-edit unit, marked, with a warn log. The review covers more than the Story rather than nothing.

edgeCases.input: A Story commit also committed ledger files (.insrc/artifacts/*.json, docs/standalone/**) and the range holds a merge.
edgeCases.expected: They are in storyChangeSet.paths but the git_diff exclude drops them, so they stay out of the review subject's changedFiles and the grounding (ISSUE-5f7a7cb9 preserved). The BUILD changeLog is unchanged in this respect: its writers pass only exact own-record paths, as today.

invariantsToPreserve.text: The Story's range base is fixed by the first build-start stamp and never moves forward.
resolveStoryRangeBase keeps returning the stamp's rangeBase first.
The grounding still marks a truncated diff and steps down to plainer attempts on DiffUnavailableError.
CliProvider callers that pass no cwd keep the inherited working directory.

Ledger files stay out of the code-review change set and grounding; that exclusion is done by git through git_diff's exclude (LEDGER_EXCLUDE_GLOBS). The BUILD changeLog's exact-path exclusions are kept as they are.

migration.stateBefore: On a clean tree, the review change set and hunks are base..HEAD from the first-stamp range base, so files a mid-build merge brought in are reviewed as Story work (changed-files.ts, grounding.ts rangeDiff). Build turns run even with an uncommitted merge. The reviewer's claude/codex subprocess inherits the daemon's working directory (cli-provider.ts complete / completeStructuredOnce call runClaude/runCodex without an ExecOverride).
migration.stateAfter: On a clean tree, the change set and hunks cover only the Story's own changes since the base: its non-merge first-parent commits plus edits made inside merge commits; files a merge brought in are absent and shared files carry only the Story's hunks. The BUILD record's changeLog lists the same Story files. Build turns return merge-in-progress while MERGE_HEAD exists. The code-review judges' CLI subprocess starts in the reviewed repository.

Update the installed daemon (daemon.update) so reviews run the new code; no stored data changes.

migration.backwardCompat: All new fields are optional and absent behaviour is unchanged: callers without opts.cwd keep the inherited working directory, git_diff without paths builds the same command line, changedFiles without a base is unchanged. Stored build-start stamps, BUILD and CR records keep their shape. Behavioural changes, all intended: (1) the code-review change set and hunks after a clean tree narrow to the Story's own changes; (2) the BUILD record's body.changeLog, derived through changedFiles with the range base by validate and by completion-record, narrows the same way; (3) build turns refuse with merge-in-progress while a merge is uncommitted. (4) The implement prompts carry the merge rule. Known limits, stated and pinned by tests: upstream brought in by fast-forward or by a committed squash merge is indistinguishable from Story commits and is reviewed as Story work.

alternativesConsidered.name: Story change units + path-limited diffs
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Derive the Story's own change units (its non-merge first-parent commits plus edits made inside merge commits) and review only their hunks.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A new helper storyChangeSet(repoPath, base) in src/workflow/runners/build/story-commits.ts lists the Story's units: each commit from `git rev-list --first-parent --no-merges base..HEAD`, and each first-parent merge whose tree differs from `git merge-tree --write-tree M^1 M^2` (edits made inside the merge). changedFiles' committed-range branch reports the units' paths. git_diff gains an optional `paths` input. The grounding's rangeDiff reviews paths no merge touched with one net base..HEAD diff limited to them, and paths a merge also touched through per-unit diffs, so no merged-in line reaches the reviewer. Build turns refuse with 'merge-in-progress' while MERGE_HEAD exists. CompletionOpts and StructuredCompletionOpts gain `cwd?`; CliProvider passes it to runClaude/runCodex; the five dimension judges pass {cwd: subject.repoPath}.
pros: Merged-in files and merged-in lines never reach the reviewer, so the bounded diff is spent only on the Story's work.
Edits folded into a merge commit are caught and reviewed instead of silently dropped.
One change set feeds the subject, the grounding and the BUILD change log, so they cannot disagree.
The range base and its first-stamp rule are untouched.
cons: A shared file is shown as several per-unit diffs rather than one net diff.
Adds a positive multi-path input to git_diff and relies on `git merge-tree --write-tree` (git 2.38+).

alternativesConsidered.name: Per-commit diffs of the Story's commits
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Review the concatenated `git show` of each non-merge first-parent Story commit instead of one net range diff.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Replace rangeDiff with a loop over `git rev-list --first-parent --no-merges base..HEAD`, collecting `git show <c>` per commit and merging per file. The change set is the union of the commits' files. The merge gate and cwd plumbing are as in a1.
pros: Exact: no merged line can appear in a hunk.
cons: A file changed by several commits appears as several partial diffs, harder to judge than its net change.
Reimplements diff parsing and the byte bound outside git_diff.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Per-commit diffs for EVERY file fragment files no merge touched, and it would drop edits made inside a merge commit; a1 uses per-unit diffs only where a merge also touched the file.

alternativesConsidered.name: Move the range base past each merge
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: When a merge commit is found in the range, re-stamp the base to the merge commit.
alternativesConsidered.approach: resolveStoryRangeBase returns the latest first-parent merge commit in base..HEAD when one exists, so the range starts after the merge.
cons: Drops every Story commit made before the merge from the review.
Contradicts the first-stamp-wins guarantee pinned by gates.test.ts CR-3.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: It loses Story work and breaks the CR-3 guarantee.
